ELUCIDATION

OF

REGIONAL REGULATION OF MAMUJU REGENCY

NUMBER 9 OF 2023

CONCERNING

WOMEN'S EMPOWERMENT AND PROTECTION

I. GENERAL ELUCIDATION

Empowerment and Protection of women currently needs to receive serious attention from all parties, including attention from the Regional Government, related to the existence of phenomena in social community life that often make them victims of violence and exploitation, they are often positioned as economic objects and are often marginalized and/or excluded in social interaction.

Law Number 23 of 2004 concerning the Elimination of Domestic Violence (Domestic Violence Law) stipulates that the state guarantees to prevent the occurrence of domestic violence, prosecute perpetrators of domestic violence, and protect victims of domestic violence. Victims of domestic violence, who are mostly women and children, must receive protection in order to avoid and be free from violence or threats of violence, torture, or treatment that degrades human dignity and worth. Therefore, the Regional Government makes regulations related to Women's Empowerment and Protection.

CHAPTER V

PROTECTION OF WOMEN

Part One

Prevention of Violence against Women

Article 19

Further provisions regarding prevention of violence against women as referred to in Article 16, Article 17 and Article 18 shall be regulated by Regent Regulation.

Article 18

Prevention of violence against women is carried out in an integrated and coordinated manner between those responsible for prevention of violence against women and the Regional Apparatus that oversees women's empowerment and child protection affairs.

CHAPTER I

GENERAL PROVISIONS

Article 1

In this regional regulation, what is meant by:

1. Region is Mamuju Regency.
2. Regional Government is the Government of Mamuju Regency.
3. Regent is the Regent of Mamuju.
4. Regional Apparatus hereinafter abbreviated as PD is an auxiliary element of the regional head and DPRD in the administration of government affairs that are the authority of the region.
5. Women's empowerment is every effort to improve physical, mental spiritual, social, knowledge and skills capabilities so that women are ready to be utilized according to their respective abilities.
6. Protection of Women is all efforts made by families, government and others aimed at women to ensure the fulfillment of women's rights as a form of respect for human rights.
7. Discrimination against women is any distinction, exclusion or restriction made on the basis of sex, which has the effect or purpose of reducing or eliminating the recognition, enjoyment or exercise of human rights and fundamental freedoms in the political, economic, social, cultural, civil or any other field by women, regardless of their marital status, on the basis of equality between men and women.
8. Violence Against Women is any action that violates, hinders, eliminates enjoyment, and neglects women's human rights.
9. Integrated Service Center for Women and Children Empowerment, hereinafter abbreviated as P2TP2A, is an integrated service center in the effort to implement women in various fields of development, as well as protection of women and children from various types of discrimination and acts of violence, including trafficking in persons, established by the government or community-based.
10. Integrated Service Unit hereinafter abbreviated as UPT is technical service units in the region that carry out integrated service functions for women and children victims of crime and/or violence, including as an information center for the implementation of women and child protection.
11. Gender is a concept that refers to the differentiation of roles, functions and responsibilities of men and women that occur as a result of and can be changed by the social and cultural conditions of society.
12. Gender Mainstreaming, hereinafter abbreviated as PUG, is a strategy built to integrate gender into men and women.
13. Regional Action Plan for Gender Mainstreaming hereinafter referred to as RANDA PUG is a planning document as a guide in efforts to implement development strategies by integrating gender into an integral dimension of planning, preparation, implementation, monitoring and evaluation of policies, programs, and development activities in the region.
14. PUG Institutional is an institution that meets the elements of PUG prerequisites, which functions effectively in a sustainable system with agreed norms in fulfilling the human rights of women and men fairly to achieve equality between women and men in all fields of development and levels of government.
15. Community institutions are institutions formed by members of the Indonesian citizen community voluntarily on the basis of shared vision, mission, profession, function, and activities to participate in development in order to achieve national goals within the framework of the Unitary State of the Republic of Indonesia based on Pancasila, consisting of religious organizations, non-governmental organizations, professional organizations, private organizations, social organizations, political organizations, mass media, and other forms of organizations.
16. Victim is a person who experiences violence and/or threats of violence within the scope of the household. 17. Community is individuals, families, groups, and social organizations and/or community organizations. 18. Task force is a coordinative institution formed by the Government of Mamuju Regency that coordinates policies, programs and activities for the protection of women and children in Mamuju Regency.

CHAPTER VII

COMMUNITY PARTICIPATION

Article 39

1. The community participates in the implementation of women's empowerment and protection.
2. Community participation as referred to in paragraph (1) shall be in the form of: a. provision of education regarding women's rights; b. provision of skills training to support the community's economy;
c. establishment of community social institutions to assist victims of violence;
d. providing information and/or reporting violence against women to law enforcement or the authorities; and/or b. participating in handling acts of violence against women.

CHAPTER II

OBLIGATIONS AND RESPONSIBILITIES OF REGIONAL GOVERNMENT

Article 2

1. The Regional Government has the obligation and responsibility for the empowerment and Protection of Women. (2) Efforts for Empowerment and Protection of Women as referred to in paragraph (1) include:a. determination of policies, programs, and activities; b. determination of implementation guidelines;
c. provision of services; andb. coordination of policies, programs and activities. (3) Efforts for Empowerment and Protection of Women as referred to in paragraph (2) are carried out in an integrated manner in accordance with applicable laws and regulations.

Paragraph 3

Social Field

Part Two

Provision of Services for Women Victims of Violence

Article 26

1. Health services as referred to in Article 24 paragraph (1) letter b shall be implemented with the following activities:a. physical and mental health examination and treatment; b. psychological examination and recovery;
c. pregnancy, childbirth, and reproductive health services;
d. medical resume and psychological examination results; e. visum et repertum and visum et psikiatrikum; f. Deoxyribo Nucleic Acid test; andg. other forms of health services needed by victims.
2. Health services for female victims shall be carried out by trained officers in a special room that is safe and comfortable.
3. Health services as referred to in paragraph (1) shall be carried out through a special mechanism of hospital-based integrated services and shall be the responsibility of the Regional Apparatus in charge of health affairs.
4. Further provisions regarding health services shall be regulated by Regent Regulation.

Paragraph 2

Legal Field

CHAPTER VIII

GUIDANCE AND SUPERVISION

Article 40

1. The Regent implements guidance and supervision of women's empowerment and protection in the Region. (2) In implementing guidance and supervision as referred to in paragraph (1), the Regent assigns the Regional Apparatus in charge of women's empowerment and child protection affairs.
3. The Regional Apparatus in charge of women's empowerment and child protection affairs as referred to in paragraph (1) shall be the coordinator for the implementation of women's empowerment and protection in the Region.

Empowerment and Protection of women currently needs to receive serious attention from all parties, including attention from the Regional Government, related to the existence of phenomena in social community life that often make them victims of violence and exploitation, they are often positioned as economic objects and are often marginalized and/or excluded in social interaction.

Law Number 23 of 2004 concerning the Elimination of Domestic Violence (Domestic Violence Law) stipulates that the state guarantees to prevent the occurrence of domestic violence, prosecute perpetrators of domestic violence, and protect victims of domestic violence. Victims of domestic violence, who are mostly women and children, must receive protection in order to avoid and be free from violence or threats of violence, torture, or treatment that degrades human dignity and worth. Therefore, the Regional Government makes regulations related to Women's Empowerment and Protection.
